findings.title: Public members endpoint response shape changed, breaking existing consumers
findings.body: `GET /groups/:id/members` used to return a bare array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` and defaults to 50 results. Any other client of this endpoint (plugins, other JS callers, API users) will break. The old automatic-group-only limit workaround is also gone, so non-automatic groups are now silently capped at 50 for callers that don't paginate. No controller spec covers the new response shape or pagination.

findings.title: Unvalidated limit and offset parameters
findings.body: `limit` comes straight from `params[:limit].to_i` with no upper bound, so a client can request an arbitrarily large page and load the whole group. A negative limit or offset can also cause a database error (negative OFFSET raises in Postgres), resulting in a 500.

findings.title: remove_member deletes via the association with a raw id and skips group-level cleanup
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` is passed an integer. This works for has_many :through, but it bypasses `Group#remove`, and any callbacks or counters tied to it. Elsewhere in the code `group.add` is used for adds, so removal is inconsistent. A non-member id is also silently ignored. The spec for this path only checks the simple case.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives an extra empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users gives 2 pages). `next` can then navigate to an offset equal to user_count and show an empty list. This should use `Math.ceil`.

findings.title: Spec uses wrong HTTP verb and routes
findings.body: The remove_member spec for automatic groups uses `xhr :put` although the route is DELETE. It passes only because controller specs bypass routing verbs. There are also no specs for the new paginated `GroupsController#members` response.

findings.title: addMembers never clears the input and ignores errors
findings.body: After `addMembers`, the usernames field is not cleared (there is a TODO), so clicking Add twice re-sends the same names. The returned promise has no failure handler, so server errors such as the 422 for automatic groups are silent.
